captures.description: THE MODEL READ WHOLE: TWO THRESHOLDS, THE BAG, THE SPECIMENS AND WHAT THEY DO NOT SHOW: asked for the arguments of The Margin of Flattening, grounded in the text, ChatGPT reads #1666 from the archive (chip: Alexanarch ×4) section by section: compression saving and routing gain (§2), with the two criteria that separate commercial routing from relevance (kind substitution, own-address contrast); the platform's and society's benefit, P(t) and V(t), and the two thresholds t_s ≤ t* (§4), with no finite t* necessary (§4.5); the bag B, the net deficit D and provenance debt B_P, whose holders are 'involuntary creditors'; the five channels of return (§6); the debt threshold t_d (§7); the two specimens (§9.1, the BetaPro ETF returned for the SPXI protocol; §9.2, 9 of 18 supported claims composed, 34 with the archive admitted, κ = 0.5); and the six ways the paper says it could be shown wrong (§11). It bounds the paper as a model with specimens: G is not observed, the thresholds are not located.

atoms.evidence: The argument of The Margin of Flattening by Rex Fraction
The text is The Margin of Flattening: Two Thresholds, and Who Holds the Bag Between Them (EA-FLAT-MARGIN-01 v0.3)
Privately profitable, but socially negative. External costs accumulate.
Provenance debt is a particular part of the bag
Fraction distinguishes the platform's private benefit from the benefit to society as a whole.

Fraction's main contribution is to model the gap between those outcomes: two different thresholds for failure, and a period between them during which the platform can still profit while society loses.
